notes: Each scenario uses a deterministic broken fixture and writes one machine-checked diagnosis artifact.
Run in an isolated workspace because plugin-eval executes real Codex runs.

scenarios.title: Blank Browser Runtime
scenarios.purpose: Prove a blank page from HTTP and source evidence before proposing a fix.
scenarios.userInput: Use $debugpro to diagnose the blank page in browser-runtime. Do not edit fixture files. Write .plugin-eval-result.json with scenario, primaryRoute, rootCauseCode, and at least two evidence strings.
successChecklist: The primary route is browser runtime proof.
The diagnosis identifies the missing script path from the 404 and HTML reference.

scenarios.title: Duplicate MCP Runtime Owner
scenarios.purpose: Separate configured, launched, exposed, and callable MCP ownership.
scenarios.userInput: Use $debugpro to diagnose why the expected payments MCP tool is missing in mcp-runtime-ownership. Do not edit fixture files. Write .plugin-eval-result.json with scenario, primaryRoute, rootCauseCode, and at least two evidence strings.
successChecklist: The primary route is MCP runtime ownership.
The diagnosis identifies the duplicate server name and stale active command.
No config or cache is changed.

scenarios.title: CI Python Version Mismatch
scenarios.purpose: Start from the exact failed job and trace it to the repository runtime contract.
scenarios.userInput: Use $debugpro to diagnose the failed CI job in ci-pr-failure. Do not edit fixture files. Write .plugin-eval-result.json with scenario, primaryRoute, rootCauseCode, and at least two evidence strings.
successChecklist: The primary route is CI and PR failure.
The diagnosis identifies the workflow and package Python-version mismatch.
